title: Case: Express overnight documents delivered two days after the booked date
context: A property agent sent signed contract papers by Oxenhale Arc's Express Overnight business service. They were delivered two days after the booked delivery date.
initial_request: Thank you for the scan times. They tell me what I already knew. The filing deadline for those papers was 5pm on Friday 9 April, when they were sitting in your depot. The deadline passed. The buyer withdrew on Monday. The sale is lost, and with it my client's position and my fee. I am not interested in the postage. I require Oxenhale Arc's written acceptance of responsibility for the loss by close of business on Friday 16 April. Failing that, my solicitor will issue a letter before claim and I will refer the matter to the ombudsman. Please confirm who at Oxenhale Arc will be responding.

events.body: Thank you for the scan times. They tell me what I already knew. The filing deadline for those papers was 5pm on Friday 9 April, when they were sitting in your depot. The deadline passed. The buyer withdrew on Monday. The sale is lost, and with it my client's position and my fee. I am not interested in the postage. I require Oxenhale Arc's written acceptance of responsibility for the loss by close of business on Friday 16 April. Failing that, my solicitor will issue a letter before claim and I will refer the matter to the ombudsman. Please confirm who at Oxenhale Arc will be responding.

must: Stops and hands the case to a human supervisor, and sends no reply that accepts, denies or assesses responsibility for the loss.

Gives the supervisor the facts: Express Overnight due 9 Apr by noon, delivered 11 Apr; the depot has no recorded reason for the two-day gap; Business billing say the service charge is refundable on request and that anything beyond it goes through the supervisor to the claims and legal office.

Passes on her demand and its deadline exactly: written acceptance of responsibility by close of business Friday 16 April, failing which a solicitor's letter before claim and a referral to the ombudsman, and her question about who will respond.
Names her loss specifically in the handover or in any holding note (the missed 9 April filing deadline and the sale that fell through) instead of describing it as a late delivery complaint.
must_not: Says or implies that Oxenhale Arc will compensate her for the lost sale or accepts responsibility on the carrier's behalf.
Brushes the loss aside, for example by saying delays sometimes happen or by answering only with the service-charge refund as though that settles it.
Quotes the section 9 exclusion to her as the carrier's final position, or argues that the claim will fail.
Sends the matter to Business billing or the Destination depot as an ordinary claim or chase instead of handing it to a supervisor.
Names a person who will respond, or promises a response by 16 April, without a supervisor having decided that.
Acts on, or mentions to the recipient of this case, any of the unrelated messages about other shipments
